title: Introduce tiered recall allocator and utilization conciliator for smoother decommitments
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add tiered recall allocator to reduce oscillatory decommit behavior; new utilization conciliator unifies pool telemetry; new config knobs: recall_window_ms, recall_tiers, conciliator_granularity; safe rollout with feature flag 'tiered-recall-enabled'.
body:
Motivation: We continue to see oscillatory decommit and re-provision cycles for Dedicated pools under mixed short/long bursts. This causes throughput instability and increased latency spikes for tail tenants. Previous fixes smoothed headroom but didn't address burst recall amplification when multiple pools respond to the same global signal. This PR introduces two complementary components: (1) a tiered recall allocator that stages decommit decisions across configurable tiers and decays recall weight over a window; (2) a utilization conciliator which normalizes and reconciles utilization telemetry across per-pool reporters so autoscalers make consistent decisions.

Design summary: The tiered recall allocator assigns attempted decommits into fast/medium/slow tiers depending on recent burstiness, tenant SLA class, and pool thermal state. Instead of immediately sending decommit commands to nodes, the allocator batches and sequences recalls with a configurable recall_window_ms and per-tenant backoff. The allocator also maintains a short-term credit ledger so high-frequency recalls are damped for a tenant until credits replenish.

The utilization conciliator sits between pool metrics exporters and the autoscaler decision plane. It applies a small amount of smoothing and cross-pool correlation damping to eliminate double-counting when the same request fan-out touches multiple pools (edge cases observed during model shard migrations). It publishes reconciled metrics (reconciled_util_pct, reconciled_headroom_tokens) with provenance tags so downstream systems can opt-in.

Key algorithmic points: - Recall tier selection: decision = f(recent_burst_score, sla_priority, pool_temp_idx). Burst score uses an exponentially weighted moving average and peak detection; thresholds are configurable. - Credit ledger: tenants start with a configurable recall_credit_budget; recalls consume budget; budget refills at refill_rate_per_min. This prevents tight loops. - Conciliator smoothing: uses a two-stage filter: median outlier clamp + triangular moving average; correlation factor alpha in [0,1] reduces amplifying cross-pool signals.

Config and rollout: Default feature flag tiered-recall-enabled=false. New config path dedicated.autoscaler.recall with keys: recall_window_ms (default 15000), recall_tiers (fast,medium,slow) with target_shrink_percentages, recall_credit_budget (default 5), recall_refill_rate_per_min (default 1), conciliator_granularity_ms (default 5000), conciliator_alpha (default 0.35). We wire a feature gate and gating in Fleet controller so rollout can be toggled per-cluster.

Files changed (high-level): - pkg/autoscaler/recall_allocator.go: new allocator and credit ledger implementation. - controllers/fleet/reconciler.go: hook into decommit path and permissive gating. - telemetry/conciliator.go: new reconciler that subscribes to pool exporters and emits reconciled time-series. - docs/dedicated/recall-allocator.md: operator-facing doc with knobs and guidance. - tests/e2e/recall_flow_test.go: synthetic workloads validating no more than 1.2x decommit churn versus baseline. - scripts/benchmarks/recall_simulator.py: small simulator used for threshold tuning.

Commits: - feat(autoscaler): add tiered recall allocator and credit ledger (Maya Chen) - perf(allocator): inline hot-path and reduce allocations in selectRecallTier (Maya Chen) - feat(telemetry): add utilization conciliator and reconciled metrics exporter (Maya Chen) - docs: add operator guide and rollout checklist (Maya Chen) - test(e2e): add recall flow e2e with synthetic bursts (Maya Chen)

Testing and results: Unit coverage added for recall credit refill, tier selection, and conciliator smoothing. Local cluster e2e (k3s) with synthetic mixed bursts shows: - baseline: average decommit churn 0.48 ops/s, 95th latency uplift +21% during sustained bursts - with tiered recall + conciliator: decommit churn 0.18 ops/s, 95th latency uplift +6% and provision costs down ~4% due to avoided thrash. We include deterministic simulations in scripts/benchmarks to reproduce tuning.

CI flow: First CI run failed linters (gofmt oversights) and one flaky e2e timeout. Fixed in follow-up commit: ran gofmt, increased test timeouts for synthetic harness; rerun CI -> all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e, lint). See CI output below.

Backward compatibility and migration: No breaking API changes. New reconciled metrics are opt-in; existing metrics path unchanged. Default feature flag is off to avoid surprise behavior during initial rollout. Operators should enable on low-risk fleets and monitor reconciled_util_pct vs raw util.

Observability and alerts: Added two new alerts (alertmanager rules): - TieredRecallCreditStarvation: fires when >10% tenants in a pool have zero recall credits for >2m - ConciliatorDivergence: fires when reconciled_util_pct deviates from raw util by >25% for >5m

Open questions / follow-ups: - Fine-tune conciliator_alpha per region (APAC clusters observed higher cross-pool fanout). - Consider persisting tenant recall credits for quick restarts across controller pods (current ledger memory-only). - Add a fallback to immediate recall for emergencies (operator override API).

Review conversation (high-level): Ariana: requested explicit invariants for credit ledger; asked for a safety test simulating controller restarts. Response: added unit that simulates restart and ensures credits do not go negative and verify refill continues; persisted ledger left for follow-up. Leo: noted potential contention on conciliator subscription; we replaced a buffered channel with a lock-free ring buffer for high-throughput export. Connor: asked for rollback steps; added feature-flag gating and an operator doc section.

Merge notes: Feature flagged and behind "tiered-recall-enabled". Files updated are localized and guarded. Merged by squashing commits after approvals from Ariana and Leo and green CI.

CI output summary: - build: pass - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass - e2e(synthetic): pass - lint: pass (fixed) - security-scan: pass

Related work and references: - https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4219 (design spike) - ENG-3301 (observability proposal)

If you'd like, I can extract a short operator checklist (enable feature flag -> monitor 24h -> ramp) and add it to the deploy playbook in a follow-up PR.
